sources.entry: Abendrot - Free open-source Mac screen warmer that cuts nighttime blue light and warms every display around local sunset.

summary.one_liner: Abendrot is a free, open-source, native macOS menu-bar app that warms each display around local sunset to reduce evening blue light.
summary.what_it_does: Abendrot is a native macOS menu-bar app that warms each connected display, using direct display warming where the Mac supports it and falling back to a screen tint when it does not. Warmth is tied to local sunset. A global hotkey lets you hold to temporarily reveal true color and release to restore warmth. An `abendrot` command-line tool drives the running app, can read live state as JSON, set warmth, and trigger a reveal, and the README says it can be used from scripts or AI coding assistants. The warmth engine is a separate open-source Swift package called WarmthKit that handles sleep, wake, and reconnects. The README says settings and usage statistics stay on the Mac, with no telemetry or account.
use_cases: reduce blue light on a Mac in the evening
night mode alternative to Night Shift
control screen warmth from the terminal or scripts
temporarily see true colors on a display
how_to_run: Download the signed, notarized .dmg from abendrot.app/download or GitHub Releases
Or install via Homebrew: brew install --cask matthewrball/tap/abendrot
Requires macOS 12 Monterey or later; universal for Apple silicon and Intel
notable: Per-display warming with screen-tint fallback when direct warming is unavailable
Global hotkey to hold and temporarily reveal true color
abendrot CLI with --json output and scriptable exit codes, controlling the running app
Local-only control: no network listener or privileged helper, per the README
No telemetry, no account, MIT licensed
caveats: Direct warming depends on what each display supports; otherwise a tint is used
Only update checks contact GitHub, per the README
General wellness tool, not a medical device
